propositions: MCP tool failures currently emit unstructured prose exceptions without machine-readable error codes, whereas the CLI already defines and emits a structured `error_envelope` discriminator that agents need to distinguish failure modes (e.g. ticket-not-found vs concurrency-mismatch).

The error code vocabulary is scattered across CLI call sites as bare string literals with no central registry, causing MCP to emit divergent ad-hoc shapes and risking codes that exist on one interface only.

Introduce a single shared classifier `error_code_for(exc)->str` plus `KNOWN_ERROR_CODES` frozenset in the library, so all three interfaces (library, CLI, MCP) draw codes from one source and remain consistent.

MCP must deliver the envelope via `McpEnvelopeError` carrying a structured `.envelope` dict, raised as `__cause__` of the `ToolError` that FastMCP wraps, and observed by tests via `pytest.raises(ToolError) as ei; ei.value.__cause__.envelope`.

The two existing MCP soft-error returns (_mcp_reads explain_criterion, _mcp_llm) must gain vocabulary error codes while preserving agent-branching fields (kind, resolution_class, retryable, diagnostic) so no signal is dropped.

CLI output must remain byte-identical, verified by regression test; the read facade must preserve the deps_failed vs ticket_not_found distinction by raising `TicketNotFoundError` only at genuine not-found sites and using `str(exc)` for human messages since library exceptions do not carry a `.message` attribute.
